extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, IP office analysts, patent statisticians, and IP professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, procedural rules, data-interpretation cautions and patentability standards used in WIPO patent statistics and analysis (e.g., patents in force, examination outcomes, pending applications, and comparability notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compare application data with grant data for same year
rubrics_metrics.description: Application data for a given year should not be compared with grant data from the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination process can take a long time and there is a time lag between application and grant dates; procedural delays make year-to-year application and grant counts non-comparable for the same calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent duration (term) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights generally last for up to 20 years from the date an application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the maximum term is typically 20 years, patentees must pay maintenance/renewal fees to keep rights; many patents lapse earlier if fees are not paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance/renewal requirement for patents in force
rubrics_metrics.description: A holder must pay a maintenance/renewal fee in order for a patent to remain valid, and may opt to let a patent lapse before the end of its full term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics on patents in force reflect this behavior: e.g., among 87 offices reporting by year of filing, approximately 39.3% of granted patents remained in force for at least 9 years after filing and about 17.8% lasted the full 20-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability standards applied by offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent offices must assess whether the claims presented in applications meet the standards of novelty, non-obviousness and industrial applicability defined in national laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory standards (novelty, inventive step/non-obviousness, industrial applicability/usefulness) drive substantive examination and consume time and resources, affecting processing volumes and pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination outcomes are compiled based on common definitions and concepts into granted, rejected, or withdrawn (abandoned) statuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2022, 87 IP offices shared data on these examination outcomes with WIPO; the figures show variation across offices (e.g., shares granted, rejected, withdrawn). Note: presentation of 'grants out of processed applications' should not be interpreted as a simple 'grant rate' without careful reading of definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications pending — official definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications pending is defined as all patent applications, at any stage in the process, awaiting a final decision by a patent office, including those applications for which applicants have not filed a request for examination (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stock of pending applications therefore includes cases not yet ready for substantive examination (e.g., awaiting a request), and increases in pending stocks at particular offices can substantially affect worldwide totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of request-for-examination rules on pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where offices have a large proportion of applications pending a request for examination, the scope to reduce the stock of applications pending is somewhat limited, as an office is unable to start the substantial examination process until an applicant has filed a request for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy or procedural differences (such as whether a request for examination is required and the timing of such requests) materially affect the ability of an office to reduce pending backlogs and should be considered when comparing pendency across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and aggregation rules for world totals
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of patent offices (e.g., 162 for applications, 155 for grants); totals include applications filed directly with national and regional offices and applications entering offices through the PCT national phase (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note the coverage count and inclusion of PCT national-phase filings when interpreting global aggregates; differences in office coverage and inclusion rules can affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data comparability / methodological breaks (country-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: China’s pre-2017 data are not comparable owing to a change in methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this break in the data series and China's large filing volumes, it is not possible to report an accurate 2017 growth rate at world level without accounting for the methodological change; analysts must treat such breaks explicitly when computing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on interpreting 'grants out of processed applications' statistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents granted out of total processed applications data presented should not be interpreted as the 'grant rate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report warns readers against simplistic interpretation of the presented distribution of outcomes; differences in definitions, processing rules, and composition of 'processed' applications across offices can mislead if labeled as a grant-rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident distinction and breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Many metrics are presented with a resident and non-resident breakdown (e.g., resident share (%) and contribution of resident and non-resident applications/grants to growth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The origin of filings and whether an application is resident or non-resident materially affect statistics (growth contributions, shares in force), and regional or office-level comparisons should account for differing resident/non-resident mixes; see glossary for formal definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force as an office-level metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of patents in force varies across offices (e.g., ranged from 11.6 years in Brazil to 6.8 years in Monaco among selected offices in 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average age is a descriptive metric for the in-force stock reflecting grant timing and maintenance behavior; comparisons over time and between offices can illuminate differences in patent portfolio vintage but require consistent office coverage.
